name: IED, EA students use theatre to learn new teaching skills

content.title: IED, EA students use theatre to learn new teaching skills
content.summary: The play demonstrated using drama as a tool for positive change in communities

media.caption: One of the scenes during the captivating performance of 'Betrayal in the City' held in Dar es Salaam campus, Tanzania
media.alt: IED, EA students use theatre to learn new teaching skills

content.text: Students from the Aga Khan University's Institute for Educational Development, East Africa (AKU-IED, EA) delivered a remarkable performance of the play "Betrayal in the City" by Kenyan playwright Francis Imbuga.

The Master of Education students, who are specializing in language and literacy, were the cast members. Directed by one of their own, Nyandwi Michael, the play shed light on oppression, corruption, nepotism, and betrayal prevalent in post-colonial Africa. The theatrical display attracted a diverse audience from various academic entities within AKU Tanzania as well as online participants from Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Pakistan and Canada.

This was not just any extra-curricular activity; it is part of their coursework. The objective was to equip students with drama and acting skills, to use as tools for active teaching and learning in their classrooms.

Dr Samuel Andema, the course facilitator, praised the performance's educational potential, emphasizing the importance of drama as a tool for positive change in communities. He implored the students to form drama clubs in their communities, not only to rejuvenate their skills but also harness the talents of their learners.

Dr Nicholas Wachira, on behalf of the Dean at IED-EA, applauded the language and literacy class for their display of critical thinking and collaboration, as well as essential 21st-century skills. The success of 'Betrayal in the City' highlighted the transformative power of art and drama, aligning with IED, EA's commitment to empowering teachers to create meaningful change.

The play's message of hope and resilience deeply touched the audience, solidifying drama as an impactful and engaging educational medium. The talented cast, including Daniel Omila, Kadondi Sofia, Juma Mwebondo and others, brought the characters to life, leaving a lasting impression on everyone.
